questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Has two strings to his bow

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: BIBLIOPHILE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e., Book admirer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Bibliophile"** refers to a person who loves or admires books and often collects them. (पुस्तक प्रेमी)

 
 
• **Example:** As a bibliophile, she spends hours browsing through old bookstores to find rare books.
 
 
 
• The correct answer, **"Book admirer"**, perfectly aligns with the meaning of "Bibliophile," as it refers to someone who has a strong affection for books. (पुस्तक प्रशंसक)
 
 
• **Example:** Being a book admirer, he has a collection of over 500 novels in his personal library.
 
 
 
• Hence, "Book admirer" is the most appropriate synonym for "Bibliophile."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Manuscript collector** (पांडुलिपि संग्राहक): A person who specifically collects handwritten or typed documents rather than books.

 
 
• **Example:** The manuscript collector specializes in acquiring rare historical documents from the 18th century.
 
 
 
• **Novel critic** (उपन्यास आलोचक): A person who analyzes and critiques novels, providing reviews and opinions.
 
 
• **Example:** The novel critic gave a detailed review of the latest bestseller.
 
 
 
• **Literature hater** (साहित्य से नफरत करने वाला): Someone who dislikes literature or books in general.
 
 
• **Example:** Despite being a literature hater, he was impressed by the storytelling in the book.

**The correct spelling of the electron-transport protein is 'Cytochrome'.**

__
 
• **Cytochrome** is a class of proteins found in the mitochondria and chloroplasts of cells. They play a key role in the electron transport chain, which is crucial for cellular respiration and energy production.
 
• The term 'cytochrome' comes from the Greek words 'kytos' meaning cell and 'chromos' meaning color, due to the colored nature of these proteins.

</ul

questions.question: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: ‘A state of temporary disuse or suspension.’
questions.solution:

__
 
• The word **‘abeyance’** means a state of temporary disuse or suspension. (अस्थायी निलंबन या स्थगन)

 
 
• **Example:** The project is in abeyance until further notice.
 
 
 
• This word is often used to describe situations where an activity, process, or rule has been paused but not ended permanently. (यह शब्द अक्सर उन परिस्थितियों में प्रयोग होता है जहाँ कोई कार्य, प्रक्रिया, या नियम अस्थायी रूप से रोका गया हो।)

Therefore, the correct answer is- **Abeyance**

• **Example:** She pressed the pause button to stop the video.

• **Example:** His insurance policy has lapsed due to non-payment.
 
 
 
• **Standstill** (ठहराव): A situation in which all activity or movement has stopped.
 
 
• **Example:** The traffic came to a standstill during the parade.

questions.question: The analyst found the correlation to be ____ insignificant to alter conclusions.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The word "**too**" is used to indicate an excessive degree or extent, which perfectly fits the context of the sentence.
 
• The sentence conveys that the correlation is excessively insignificant to make any changes to the conclusions.
 
• **Options 2, 3, 4**, and 5 are grammatically or contextually incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The analyst found the correlation to be **too**__ insignificant to alter conclusions."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: Her claim was logical; ___, it ignored the latest survey.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**nevertheless**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The conjunction "**nevertheless**" is used to indicate a contrast or an exception in a logical sequence.
 
• The sentence highlights that the claim was logical, but it overlooked an important detail (the latest survey), which makes "**nevertheless**" the correct choice.
 
• **Options 1 (nonetheless)** and **Option 2 (alternatively)** are inappropriate because they do not fit the context or convey the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4 (thereby)** is incorrect, as it suggests causation, which is not implied in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Her claim was logical; **nevertheless**__, it ignored the latest survey."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "nonetheless"** is similar in meaning to "nevertheless," but in this context, "nevertheless" is more appropriate for formal writing.
 
• **Option 2: "alternatively"** suggests an alternative option, which is not relevant to the given sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "thereby"** indicates causation and is unsuitable for the sentence structure.
</ul

questions.question: Change to passive: We shall have dispatched the invitations before Monday morning.

options.text: The invitations shall have dispatched before Monday morning.
The invitations shall have had been dispatched before Monday morning.
The invitations shall have be dispatched before Monday morning.
The invitations shall have been dispatched before Monday morning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence. 
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "We shall have dispatched the invitations before Monday morning." 
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the invitations" at the beginning. 
 
• Change the active verb form "shall have dispatched" to "shall have been dispatched" (future perfect passive). 
 
• Ensure the time phrase "before Monday morning" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The invitations shall have been dispatched before Monday morning."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1: **"The invitations shall have dispatched before Monday morning." – Incorrect passive form. 
 
• **Option 2: **"The invitations shall have had been dispatched before Monday morning." – Incorrect verb tense. 
 
• **Option 3: **"The invitations shall have be dispatched before Monday morning." – Incorrect verb form. 
</ul

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The committee’s attempt to delay the verdict (1) / was blamed partly on public pressure (2) / and partly due to procedural confusion (3) / that emerged recently. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the phrase "**partly due to procedural confusion**" in Part 3.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**and partly because of procedural confusion**."
 
• The usage of "**due to**" is incorrect here, as it does not fit the parallel structure with "**partly on public pressure**."
 
• The sentence should maintain grammatical consistency and clarity by using "**because of**" instead of "**due to**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The committee’s attempt to delay the verdict was blamed partly on public pressure and partly because of procedural confusion that emerged recently."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part 1:** "*The committee’s attempt to delay the verdict*" is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 2:** "*was blamed partly on public pressure*" is also correct and does not contain any grammatical errors.
 
• **Part 4:** "*that emerged recently*" is correct and does not need revision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: According to the passage, which quality is most essential for entrepreneurs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Entrepreneurship requires individuals to face unpredictability, adapt quickly, and operate without guaranteed earnings.***

 
 
• These qualities highlight the need for **resilience**—the ability to persist and recover from setbacks, which is most essential for entrepreneurs according to the passage.
 
 
 
• ***Other qualities such as obedience, compliance, and predictability***
 
 
• These are more aligned with traditional jobs, where stability and clearly defined roles are emphasized, not with entrepreneurship.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2 (Resilience).**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Obedience):** Incorrect, as entrepreneurship values independent thinking over obedience.
 
• **Option 3 (Compliance):** Incorrect, since entrepreneurs often challenge norms and adapt rather than simply comply.
 
• **Option 4 (Predictability):** Incorrect, as entrepreneurship is inherently unpredictable.

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate replacement:

He is looking forward __**to meet you soon**__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "looking forward to" is always followed by a gerund (verb + ing) and not the infinitive form (to + verb).
 
• The correct phrase should be "to meeting you soon" instead of "to meet you soon."
 
• Using the gerund form ensures grammatical correctness and conveys the intended meaning properly.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1: to meeting you soon**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He is looking forward to meeting you soon."*

questions.question: Direct to indirect: “Justice must be delivered at any cost,” said the judge.

options.text: The judge said that justice should be delivered at any cost.
The judge said that justice must be delivered at any cost.
The judge said one must deliver justice.
The judge said justice is delivered at any cost.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The judge said that justice must be delivered at any cost.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **“Justice must be delivered at any cost” becomes “justice must be delivered at any cost.”**
 
 
• The modal verb “must” is retained in indirect speech to preserve the sense of obligation.
 
• No change in tense is required as the statement is a universal truth.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Direct: “said”
 
• Converted to: “said that,” introducing the indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is converted into indirect speech without quotation marks.
 
• “That” is used as a conjunction to link the reporting clause to the reported speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The judge said that justice must be delivered at any cost.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** “The judge said that justice should be delivered at any cost.” 
 
 
• Incorrect modal verb: “should” changes the sense of obligation and weakens the statement.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** “The judge said one must deliver justice.” 
 
 
• Altered meaning: the emphasis on “justice at any cost” is lost.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** “The judge said justice is delivered at any cost.” 
 
 
• Incorrect tense: “is delivered” changes the statement’s meaning to a present ongoing action.

questions.question: Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph:1. It involves a systematic inquiry to discover new insights or validate established ones.2. Research forms the base of scientific and academic development.3. It can either expand theoretical understanding or address practical issues.4. The outcomes are recorded and reviewed to ensure reliability.
questions.solution:

• "Research forms the base of scientific and academic development."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1 follows** as it defines what research involves:
 
 
• "It involves a systematic inquiry to discover new insights or validate established ones."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 3 comes next** as it elaborates on research's scope and purpose:
 
 
• "It can either expand theoretical understanding or address practical issues."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 4 concludes** by describing what happens to the outcomes:
 
 
• "The outcomes are recorded and reviewed to ensure reliability."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **2, 1, 3, 4**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Research forms the base of scientific and academic development. It involves a systematic inquiry to discover new insights or validate established ones. It can either expand theoretical understanding or address practical issues. The outcomes are recorded and reviewed to ensure reliability."
